page_title: AutoFDO: Automatic Feedback-Directed Optimization for Warehouse-Scale Applications

sources.entry: AutoFDO: Automatic Feedback-Directed Optimization for Warehouse-Scale Applications - Defines the address-to-source mapping with discriminators that lets a stale production profile still drive FDO.

summary.title: AutoFDO: Automatic Feedback-Directed Optimization for Warehouse-Scale Applications
summary.one_liner: AutoFDO uses sampled hardware performance counter profiles from production machines, which are stale by design, to drive feedback-directed optimization at warehouse scale.
takeaways: AutoFDO samples hardware performance monitors on production machines to guide compiler optimization.
Profiles are stale by design; compiler features are added so speedups hold across releases.
Reported result: a geomean 10.5% improvement on Google's benchmarks, reaching 85% of traditional FDO gains.
Enabling it requires only adding some flags to the release build, and it is deployed to hundreds of Google binaries.
summary.summary: The page describes AutoFDO, a Google system that simplifies deploying feedback-directed optimization by sampling hardware performance monitors on production machines and feeding those profiles back into compilation. Because profiles are stale by design, the compiler gains are built around features that keep speedups stable across releases. The page reports a geomean 10.5% improvement on its benchmarks, 85% of traditional FDO gains, and deployment to hundreds of binaries with only extra release-build flags needed. It also states AutoFDO increased FDO users at Google 8X and that over half of CPU cycles now run in some form of FDO-optimized binaries.
